description: Cross-language conformance fixture catalog. NOTE: the $schema above is editor/IDE only — sce-build/src/conformance.rs hand-rolls runtime validation; the JSON schema is never consulted at codegen time. Each entry declares a fixture's structural metadata (kind, arg types, output shape) so sce-codegen can render per-language test harnesses from a single source. The oracle values — expected outputs — live in numerical_reference.json. Adding a new fixture requires (1) an SCXML file under tests/forge/resources/, (2) an entry here, and (3) an expected-value entry in numerical_reference.json. No language-specific test code should ever need to be hand-written.

kinds.interpolation: Pure lookup table with numeric interpolation. Struct::lookup(args) -> scalar. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.transform: Value transform. Free function(s) compute_*(args) -> scalar or multi-output. Reference section: pure_functions. A transform that reads a field through previous() is driven through its holder instead: the harness derives that from the document, runs the oracle's `sequence` of activations from a new holder and again after reset(), and compares every output of each activation by its compound_outputs key. Reference section: stateful_transforms.
kinds.condition: Pure boolean predicate. Free function <name>(args) -> bool. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.filter: Stateful signal filter. Instance::update(input) -> output, one output per sequence step. Reference section: stateful_filters.
kinds.observer: Stateful event observer. Instance::update(input) -> event queue, zero-or-more events per step. Reference section: observers.
kinds.procedure: Pure procedure result. Language-specific binding returns ProcedureResult{completed, final_state}. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.lookup: Finite key→value mapping. Free function lookup_<name>(key) -> V|Option<V>. Numeric outputs use direct comparison; string outputs return language-specific enums verified via oracle string matching. Reference section: pure_functions (numeric) or string_lookups (enum).
kinds.timer: Periodic timer, ONE per document (SCE_FORGE.md 4.10). Generated class wraps a single ITimer HAL instance and exposes start() / cancel() plus a hook per declared lifecycle element. Conformance injects a recording mock, calls start(), verifies the registered period against period_us, and verifies callback dispatch by triggering the mock's stored callback and checking the recording handler received fire<FireEvent>(). Reference section: timers. The oracle is the SEQUENCE of calls the generated class makes on the injected timer plus the handler call a firing routes to, because that surface — start / cancel / onReset / onCancel-exit and a compile-time period constant — is the one all six language arms share.
kinds.enum: Named value vocabulary. Generated as the language's own enum type with the declared values. Conformance compares the NUMBER each variant carries, because that number is on a wire; the spelling differs by language (GeneralReject in C++/Rust/Go, GENERAL_REJECT in Python/Kotlin), so the oracle keys on the source name the document writes and each fragment applies its own case filter — the same contract codec uses for field names. Reference section: enums.
kinds.validator: Stateful data validator. Instance::validate(args...) returns a struct whose layout is declared per fixture under `output` as a list of {name, type, compare} entries; the fragment iterates those fields to build per-field assertions, which keeps the forge product's return-struct shape (currently always {valid, reason}) out of the five per-language fragment templates. Internal sample memory (for rate-of-change checks) advances only on a successful validation, so oracle sequences exercise range / ROC / plausibility branches and the state-non-update rule. Reference section: validators.
kinds.codec: Byte-layout codec. Generated struct exposes `encode()` returning the raw byte vector and a static `decode(raw)` returning the typed struct (wrapped in the language's optional). Oracle cases are `{decoded, encoded}` pairs exercising round-trip symmetry in both directions. Field layout lives in SCXML (sce:byte, sce:bit-offset, sce:bit-size, sce:default-endian); the manifest entry only mirrors field names and canonical types so fragments can iterate them. Field names use SCXML source case (camelCase) as the canonical key across oracle and manifest; each per-language fragment applies its own case filter (Rust/Python snake_case, Go PascalCase, C++/Kotlin as-is camelCase). Reference section: codecs.
kinds.algorithm: RFC §5.A pure free function with bounded loops. Free function `<name>(args) -> scalar` with optional bytes parameters lowering to the language's native byte-stream view (`sce_forge_bytes_t` on C11, `&[u8]` on Rust). Cross-(Rust, C11) byte-equivalence is the §A6 acceptance gate; A6 wires the two CRC16-CCITT-FALSE fixtures (bit-by-bit + table-fold) through the conformance harness so any future codegen drift fails ctest. Reference section: pure_functions.

canonical_types.description: Canonical arg/input/output types. Each per-language template maps these to its own type system (e.g. u16 -> uint16 in Go, UShort in Kotlin, std::uint16_t in C++). `bytes` is the variable-length byte sequence; in args it represents a `sce_forge_bytes_t` view on C11 / `&[u8]` on Rust.
